title: Quantum-enhanced mechanical sensing with machine-learning estimation
authors: Finn Müßigbrodt, Andraž Omahen, Q. Rumman Rahman, Giulio Corazza, Yiwen Chu, Matteo Fadel
abstract: Massive mechanical oscillators couple directly to forces, accelerations and gravity, making them attractive probes of new physics and of quantum mechanics at macroscopic scales. Pushing sensitivities beyond the standard quantum limit for signals of unknown phase requires non-Gaussian quantum states, whose metrological advantage has so far been confined to lighter systems such as trapped ions. Here we operate a microgram-scale acoustic mode of a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator as a phase-insensitive quantum-enhanced sensor. A transmon qubit prepares the mode in Fock states of up to seven phonons by optimal control, and resolves its phonon-number distribution after interaction with a weak resonant signal. Bayesian analysis yields a Fisher information five times the vacuum value, a 7.0 dB gain in signal-amplitude sensitivity over any classical probe state, irrespective of its energy, currently limited by state preparation infidelities. We then train a neural network on the measured sensor response to perform Bayesian estimation without any analytical model of the system, showing the same sensitivity gain with half the systematic bias. Our results establish acoustic resonators prepared in non-Gaussian states as quantum-enhanced probes for high-frequency gravitational waves, dark matter and wave-function collapse.
summary: This research demonstrates quantum-enhanced mechanical sensing by utilizing a microgram-scale acoustic resonator coupled to a qubit. By preparing the mechanical mode in non-Gaussian Fock states, the authors achieved a 7.0 dB improvement in signal sensitivity over classical limits. The use of machine learning to estimate the signal further validates this quantum advantage by minimizing systematic model errors.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of pushing quantum measurement sensitivities beyond the Standard Quantum Limit (SQL) for phase-insensitive signals using macroscopic mechanical oscillators.
main_result: They demonstrated a 7.0 dB sensitivity gain in signal-amplitude estimation using a microgram-scale acoustic resonator prepared in non-Gaussian Fock states. Furthermore, they showed that a model-free neural network estimator can reproduce this quantum advantage while significantly reducing systematic bias.
method: The methodology combines quantum state preparation (Fock states via optimal control), quantum sensing protocols involving weak resonant drives, and advanced estimation techniques including Bayesian analysis and neural network training.
model_or_system: The physical system is a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator (HBAR) coupled to a transmon qubit (cQAD device). The sensing relies on preparing the mechanical mode in Fock states, which are then probed by a weak resonant signal.
key_observables: Fisher information, signal-amplitude sensitivity gain (7.0 dB), phonon-number distribution $P(\mu)$, and the Hellinger distance $D_H^2$.
important_parameters: HBAR effective mass ($\approx 16 \mu	ext{g}$), Qubit/Phonon frequencies ($\approx 5.07-5.08 	ext{ GHz}$), and the probe state Fock number ($|kangle$).
main_assumptions: The initial estimation relied on a parametrized model, which was overcome by using a model-free neural network estimator. The quantum enhancement peaks for the $|4angle$ state due to state preparation imperfections.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device setup and sensing protocol, showing measured phonon-number populations for different Fock states before and after displacement, and comparing the squared Hellinger distance for various displacements.
paper_structure: The paper details the quantum mechanical model (Hamiltonians), the sensing protocol involving Fock state preparation and weak signal interaction, the theoretical limits using Fisher information, and finally, the experimental demonstration using both model-based and model-free (NN) estimation techniques.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes quantum metrology into the macroscopic mechanical domain, demonstrating how quantum resources (non-Gaussian states) can enhance sensing beyond classical limits in a solid-state platform.
